posts.angle: What running lead campaigns across four countries taught me about the gap between cheap leads and real buyers.
posts.heldBecause: selling day — you approve anything that makes an offer
posts.hook: 7,341 lead-form submissions. Nine Meta ad accounts. Four countries. Here is what the numbers actually show, and what they don't.
posts.body:
7,341 lead-form submissions. Nine Meta ad accounts. Four countries.

Here is what the numbers actually show, and what they don't.

A lead-form submission just means someone filled a form on an ad and Meta logged it against that ad. That's the whole definition. Nothing about intent, budget, or whether they ever buy.

Say a Tirupur apparel manufacturer runs a wholesale campaign. 19 UK buyers responded to an ad and form that both stated a 200-piece minimum order, at under $6 an enquiry. That's a qualified question, answered cheaply.

Compare that to Nova Attire: 4,248 wholesale buyer leads at ₹16.58 each, across six campaigns, total spend ₹70,444. In their own words, translated from Tamil — within ten days, 150-plus enquiries came in, and they were converting many of them.

But how many of those 4,248 became actual orders? That number was never captured. Nothing sent it back into Meta.

Cheap leads and real buyers are two different measurements. One lives in Ads Manager. The other lives in a sales register nobody connected back to the ad.

If you're running lead ads and only tracking cost per lead, you're tracking half the story.

Free resource on my site: an audit checklist for what to track after the lead, not just before it.

#leadgen #metaads #d2c

slides.text: 7,341 leads. Four countries. One gap nobody measured.
A cheap lead can still be a stranger. That gap costs real money.
A lead-form submission just means someone filled a form on an ad.
That's it. Nothing about budget, intent, or whether they ever buy.
19 UK buyers answered an ad stating a 200-piece minimum, under $6 each.
That's a qualified question, answered cheap. Most campaigns never ask one.
Nova Attire: 4,248 wholesale leads at ₹16.58 each across six campaigns.
Their words, translated from Tamil: within ten days, 150-plus enquiries came in.
But how many of those 4,248 became orders? That number was never captured.
Cost per lead lives in Ads Manager. Buyer count lives in a sales register nobody connected.
The gap between cheap leads and real buyers isn't the ad cost. It's the missing link back.
Track cost per lead, and you're tracking half the story.
